title: Lender completes £4.5m Dorset commercial refinance in seven days
summary:
TAB has completed two linked bridging facilities totalling £4.5 million to refinance existing debt on commercial properties in Poole and Bournemouth. The transactions were completed within seven days of the initial enquiry, despite what the lender described as a complex legal and beneficial ownership structure.

title: Property listings near traditional pubs across England
summary:
Five residential properties located near established public houses across England have been listed for sale, with prices ranging from £595,000 to £1.2 million. The listings span locations from Leicestershire and Cornwall to London, representing different segments of the regional property market.

title: Glasgow PBSA scheme secures £35.5m development finance
summary:
A former office building in Glasgow will be converted into a 288-bed purpose-built student accommodation scheme following a £35.5m development loan from Atelier to MCR Property Group. The 16-month facility will fund the permitted development conversion into 163 studio apartments and 125 cluster rooms.

title: Eviction cases rise 21% following Renters’ Rights Act
summary:
Landlord eviction cases have increased 21% since the introduction of the Renters' Rights Act, according to new Ministry of Justice statistics. The figures show accelerated possession claims surged 68% during the same period, prompting calls for urgent court system reforms.

title: Leasehold campaigner calls freeholders ‘property mafia’
summary:
Leasehold reform campaigner Harry Scoffin has described freeholders as a "property mafia" in BBC Radio 4 comments, whilst criticising recent parliamentary reforms as insufficient. The Residential Freehold Association disputed the characterisation, citing 93% leaseholder satisfaction rates.

The post Leasehold campaigner calls freeholders ‘property mafia’ appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Friday 13th sees fewest property completions, data shows
summary:
Analysis of Land Registry data spanning three decades shows Friday the 13th records the lowest number of property completions of any Friday. Properties numbered 13 are valued £3,400 below average, whilst number one homes command a £27,700 premium.

The post Friday 13th sees fewest property completions, data shows appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Government unveils leasehold service charge reforms
summary:
The Government has published new regulations to reform leasehold service charges in England, with the first measures coming into force on 1st April 2027. The reforms will strengthen leaseholders' rights to receive detailed information about service charges and challenge costs they consider unfair.

The post Government unveils leasehold service charge reforms appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Cotswolds developer secures £1.3m overdraft facility
summary:
Alternative Bridging Corporation has provided a £1.3 million overdraft facility to a Cotswolds-based housebuilder experiencing cash flow pressure due to delays between property reservations and completed sales. The facility, structured at 55% loan-to-value, allows the developer to draw funds as needed rather than taking the full amount immediately.

title: Lender provides £900,000 bridge on listed properties
summary:
Precise Mortgages has completed a £900,000 bridging loan secured against two Grade II listed properties in London, enabling clients to purchase a retirement home in Sussex. The 12-month loan was arranged by broker Yomo Finance and completed 25 days after the initial offer.

The post Lender provides £900,000 bridge on listed properties appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Wealth manager calls for scrapping of mansion tax
summary:
The chief executive of deVere Group has called for the government to scrap the High Value Council Tax Surcharge before its implementation in April 2028. The tax will apply to homes in England valued above £2 million, affecting fewer than 1% of properties.
